keyFindings.description: 'the smallest role's memory budget may be well under a gigabyte' is below anything in evidence, and the note states it as a hedge rather than a measurement. The smallest memory limit recorded anywhere for a role is 1Gi: Legion's defaultResources and golden/root.json give 1Gi to the architect, planner and merger, and dispatch://INFRA-51/comment/12ce8e6b-0e14-4ff4-9cb2-b48306b15906 reads a live issue pod created after the evening's applies with exactly 1Gi/1Gi/6Gi/6Gi/4Gi/1Gi, noting the stack sets no memory at all. The sub-gigabyte figure comes from 512Mi in dispatch://INFRA-51/comment/a9f52454, which is the ephemeral-storage rebalance - that comment opens on tester evictions ('exceeded its local ephemeral storage limit "1Gi"') and its 10Gi total is the per-pod ephemeral ceiling of dispatch://INFRA-31 - and I was the one who read it as memory in round 2. Rewrite to what is in evidence: the smallest memory limit recorded for a role is 1Gi, and a cache moved onto a tmpfs can exceed that. The warning keeps its force without a number nobody has measured for memory.

'Read your own container's limits rather than any number here' is an instruction the note's own reader cannot carry out, and the rest of the same sentence says so: from inside, the only readable counter is the sandbox's /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes (20,401,094,656 bytes here, equal to free -k's total, which the later paragraph warns against mistaking for a limit), and the per-container limits are in the pod spec, which needs cluster access. A note whose advice cannot be followed from where its reader sits is the defect class this file documents. Rewrite to say where the answer actually is - the pod spec, through whoever can read the cluster, or the deployment's own record - and to say plainly that it is not readable from inside the container.
